text:
alex: Quick sync — proposal attached: latency-first tenant lanes for high-SLA customers. Goal: isolate hot paths so high-tier apps consistently hit low tail latency. Thoughts?

mika: +1 on the goal. Two runtime constraints to call out: KV-cache locality and batching behavior will change, need API hooks to prefer local shards.

sam: From infra: isolating lanes = reserved GPU pools. Ballpark cost uplift +18-25% for peak tail workloads. Can prototype with a small reserved commit.

nina: Customers keep asking for predictable p95. Suggest adding launch criterion: no more than 10% error-budget regression for co-tenants when lanes enabled.

alex: Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- p50 < 30ms and p95 < 60ms on a 1k-sample short-prompt workload
- error-rate delta vs baseline < 10%
- cost-per-token uplift < 25% (configurable per-customer tier)

mika: Ops hooks we need: per-tenant telemetry, lane tagging in traces, and automatic fallback to standard lane when capacity/latency thresholds breach.

sam: Fallback policy ideas: 1) soft degrade -> switch to quantized model variant, 2) region failover -> route to compatible region, 3) throttled bursts. Recommend canary: 5 customers for 2 weeks.

nina: Also require: SLO dashboard, a clear runbook for evictions, and a customer comms template (who to notify, SLA expectations).

alex: Tentative timeline: Q3 spec + infra spike, Q4 pilot (canary customers), Q1 next-year GA. Major known blockers?

mika: Blocker: kernel-selection & runtime affinity workstream — need an RFC + perf toy to validate scheduling heuristics.

sam: Blocker: procurement/commit for reserved GPU capacity in EU region for the pilot. Need cost sign-off.

alex: Action items: @mika draft RFC by EOD Fri, @sam produce cost & commit options by Monday, @nina start customer comms template and pilot candidate list.

deploy-bot: Reminder: roadmap-lanes sync scheduled 2023-05-05 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent).

alex: Thanks all — I'll fold these notes into the public roadmap doc: https://redwood.internal/roadmaps/latency-lanes and tag owners. :thumbsup:
